subject: Praxis Health — privacy addendum feasibility & migration checklist
messages:
From: Elena Ramos <elena.ramos@praxis-health.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: contracts@praxis-health.com
Date: Sun, 20 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood privacy addendum — initial scope + dataflow

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks for taking this on. Attached is our standard DPA redline template and a high-level dataflow diagram for the integration between our EHR and the Redwood inference endpoints. A few items we want to confirm up front so Legal and our DPO can sign off quickly: 

- BAA applicability: we treat PHI at-rest in our EHR; we need confirmation that Redwood can operate under a Business Associate Agreement for the features we plan to use (real-time summarization + de-identification helpers).
- Subprocessor residency: our policy requires that any subprocessor storing or caching patient-identifiable content be either US-resident or covered by an acceptable contractual transfer mechanism. Are your public cloud subprocessors covered?
- KMS & key control: we prefer customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-key) for production. Is a KMS/HSM integration possible for the Dedicated or Private deployment?
- Data retention and audit logs: we need explicit retention windows and per-request audit logging for the pilot.

For timeline, Compliance would like a statement of feasibility and a short migration checklist by Wed (22 Jun). Can you confirm who on your side will own the technical checklist items?

Best,
Elena Ramos
Sr. Counsel, Privacy & Compliance
Praxis Health Systems

Attachments: praxis_dpa_draft_v1.pdf, praxis_dataflow_v1.svg

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ramos <elena.ramos@praxis-health.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood privacy addendum — initial scope + dataflow

Elena — thanks for the packet. Quick notes while we review the DPA redline: please see inline questions in the Drive link (shared). High level answers to the four bullets so you can flag internally: 

1) BAA: Redwood supports signing a BAA for covered PHI usage under our Hosted and Dedicated offerings. For Private (on-prem) we can accept a customer-attested environment. The BAA scope will list allowed model usages (generation, embeddings, routing).

2) Subprocessors: Our runtime uses a mix of managed cloud providers for telemetry and storage of transient KV caches. We can commit to US-only residency for any cached token material for your pilot; long-term cross-region routing can be disabled. We'll provide a subprocessor list and addendum.

3) KMS/HSM: Customer-managed keys are supported for Dedicated and Private. For Hosted, we offer envelope encryption with customer KMS for keys (bring-your-own-key pattern) but full HSM-backed signing is currently available only on Redwood Private.

4) Retention & audit logs: We can configure per-route retention windows and emit per-request audit events with request IDs and redaction flags. The audit payload can be delivered to your SIEM via secure webhook or pushed to your cloud project.

Marcus and Mina — can one of you own the technical checklist (networking, KMS onboarding, subnet peering, and pilot routing) and turn around a 1-page checklist for Elena by Wed?

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Strategic Accounts (Healthcare)
Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ramos <elena.ramos@praxis-health.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood privacy addendum — initial scope + dataflow

Elena — I can own the technical checklist. Draft below is what I'll deliver as a one-page pilot runbook. Please flag any must-haves.

--- Pilot technical checklist (draft) ---
1) Environment selection: Dedicated GPU pool (recommended) or Private (on-prem) if Praxis requires full network isolation.
2) KMS onboarding: Provide service account and KMS key_arn for envelope encryption. For Private, coordinate HSM cert exchange.
3) Network: For Dedicated, set up VPC peering + security rules. For Private, provide egress whitelist for only Redwood update endpoints.
4) Dataflow handling: Disable persistent KV caching for PHI routes; enable prefix-KV caching only for de-identified tokens.
5) Retention & logging: Set route retention to 7 days for pilot; configure webhook to your SIEM (endpoint + signing key).
6) Subprocessor list: We'll include a signed subprocessor statement and commit to US residency for caches for the pilot.
7) SLA/backups: Define RTO/RPO expectations in addendum.
8) Test plan: 3-day smoke with synthetic records, then 10-day pilot with a consented cohort.

I will attach this checklist and a quick network diagram to the Drive link and share a DocuSign-ready DPA redline by EOD.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: praxis_pilot_checklist_v1.pdf

From: Elena Ramos <elena.ramos@praxis-health.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: contracts@praxis-health.com, DPO Team <dpo@praxis-health.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood privacy addendum — initial scope + dataflow

Marcus/Vanessa — this is exactly what Compliance needed. A few follow-ups: 

- Please mark which checklist items require network changes that our infra team will need to schedule maintenance for (we have a freeze window next week).
- On KMS: we'll send the key_arn for testing but will need a timeline for HSM cert exchange if Private is chosen.
- Subprocessor statement: can you include a commitment window (e.g., we will notify Praxis of any subprocessor changes 30 days in advance)?

If you can add those three clarifications and share the DocuSign-ready DPA by EOD tomorrow, we can route to Legal and the DPO and schedule the pilot kickoff.

Elena Ramos
Sr. Counsel, Privacy & Compliance
Praxis Health Systems
